decisions.statement: A pool with no account left is sent to the fallback provider before anything else.
The fallback is reached the moment no account is left rather than after a wait.
A fallback that answers is served, whatever status that answer carries.
A fallback there is none of leaves the answer empty as it was.
A fallback that throws leaves the answer empty rather than answering 502.
A fallback attempt carries no bearer and no account of the pool.
A fallback attempt asks for the model the fallback provider states.
A pool with no account and no fallback is answered empty with the trail `-`.
A pool with no account and no fallback is forwarded nowhere.
An account with no fresh token is forwarded with whatever token the client sent.
A fallthrough with no fresh token names the account that was chosen.
Every attempt has the token read for the account being tried.
Every attempt goes through `retry` so a dropped connection is tried again.
A forward that throws is answered 502.
A forward that throws is written about on the error seam.
An account is added to the trail before that account is tried.
A 429 is handed to `server-error-retry` before any other handler.
A 500 is handed to `server-error-retry` before any other handler.
A 502 is handed to `server-error-retry` before any other handler.
A 503 is handed to `server-error-retry` before any other handler.
A 529 is handed to `server-error-retry` before any other handler.
A server error lasting through its retries is served as the answer.
A 403 is handed to `permission-denied-rebind`.
A 400 is handed to `forced-tool-choice` once for a whole request.
A tool choice rewritten is replayed at the same account.
A 404 on an extended-context body replays the base sibling at the same account.
A base sibling is replayed once for a whole request.
A body downshifted to its base sibling is read again for the fable model.
The body of a 404 being replayed is cancelled rather than left open.
A 404 with no base sibling to try is handed to `model-unavailable-rebind`.
A 401 is handed to `auth-failed-retry` once for each account.
A 401 answered a newer credential is replayed at the same account.
A status under 400 that is no 429 is served.
A status at or above 400 that no handler took is written to the error seam.
An answer on a trail of one account names that account alone.
An answer on a longer trail names every account the request reached.
Every 429 is written about with its error type and its capacity class.
A 429 on a fast-mode request strips the speed and the beta before any mark.
A fast-mode strip is made once for a whole request.
A fast-mode strip replays the same account.
A 429 the capacity classifier calls not-capacity is served rather than rebound.
A 429 on a fable request rebinds without marking the account at its limit.
A 429 on any other request marks the account at its limit before rebinding.
The `retry-after` header of a 429 reaches the act marking the account.
Every 429 asks for the account's usage to be read again.
The usage read is asked for without waiting on the answer.
A usage read that rejects is written about rather than left unhandled.
The accounts already tried are kept from every later choice.
A choice answering an account already tried is answered empty as `looped`.
A choice answering no account is answered empty as `no-viable-account`.
An account chosen with no fresh token is answered empty as `no-fresh-token`.
An empty answer names the trail of accounts the request reached.
A 429 body is read to text the once through `peek-response`.
The map of reasons to accounts lives as long as one request's run.
A caller hands in the choice of an account.
A caller hands in the read answering a fresh credential.
A caller hands in the forward every attempt is sent through.
A caller hands in the read answering the fallback provider.
A caller hands in each act that changes an account's allowance.
Nothing here loads a module to decide which handler a status reaches.
Nothing here reads a page.
Nothing here reads a clock.
Nothing here waits between attempts at two accounts.
Nothing here writes a transport row.
No answer here is built from a body this module invented.
`tools/lib/model-gateway/pick-pipeline.ts` leaves the usage read's rejection unhandled.
Every line written here goes to the console rather than to a seam.
A 502 answered for a transport error has no body naming the failure.
A request replayed at the same account is added to the trail a second time.
The loop is bounded by the accounts filed rather than by a ceiling of its own.
A body already sent upstream is sent again without asking whether the second send is safe.
A request rebuilt for a fast-mode replay has no body of its own.

definition: one request carried from account to account until an answer comes back
